summary.text: The solar wind is a stream of charged particles released from the Sun's outermost atmospheric layer, the corona.
This plasma mostly consists of electrons, protons and alpha particles, and it varies in density, temperature and speed over time.
Its particles escape the Sun's gravity because of the corona's heat, and related phenomena include the aurora and comet tails that always point away from the Sun.

facts.label: Speed far out
facts.value: 250-750 km/s, faster than fast magnetosonic waves

facts.label: Slowdown point
facts.value: Flow stops being supersonic at the termination shock

items.prompt: A comet loops around the Sun and heads back out into space. Which way will its tail point?

options.label: Behind the comet, along its path
Toward the Sun, pulled by gravity
Away from the Sun, whichever way the comet travels
Sideways, along the comet's orbit

items.explain: Comet tails always point away from the Sun, regardless of the direction in which the comet is travelling, because the Sun emits a steady stream of particles.

items.prompt: The Sun's gravity is strong, yet a stream of particles still flows away from it. What lets those particles break free?

options.label: Their high energy, from the corona's high temperature
A pull from the planets as they pass
Gravity dropping to zero just above the surface
Their being lighter than any gas on Earth

items.explain: The particles escape the Sun's gravity because of their high energy, a result of the high temperature of the corona.

items.prompt: The corona is so hot that its pressure cannot be held back by gravity alone. What did Parker conclude the gas must do?

options.label: Stay put in a still shell around the Sun
Flow outward, speeding up to supersonic beyond a critical point
Fall back and sink into the Sun
Flow outward at one steady slow speed

items.explain: Parker argued a million-degree corona cannot remain static: pressure forces must drive an expanding flow that goes from subsonic near the Sun to supersonic beyond a critical point.

items.prompt: A scientist in the early 1900s finds the northern lights almost never switch off. What did he conclude about particles from the Sun?

options.label: They arrive only in rare bursts
They arrive only during solar eclipses
They are all positively charged
Earth is being continually bombarded by them

items.explain: Birkeland's surveys showed auroral activity was almost uninterrupted, so he concluded the Earth was continually bombarded by particles from the Sun.

items.prompt: Some early scientists thought the Sun sends out only one kind of electric charge. What did Birkeland propose instead?

options.label: Both negative electrons and positive ions
Only electrons, the lightest particles
Only positive ions
Neutral atoms with no charge

items.explain: Birkeland proposed that the rays from the Sun are neither exclusively negative nor positive but of both kinds.

items.prompt: In 1859 a bright flash on the Sun was followed a day later by a powerful geomagnetic storm. What is the storm now attributed to?

options.label: A comet's tail sweeping past Earth
A sudden dimming of the Sun
A coronal mass ejection arriving near Earth
Earth passing through a sunspot

items.explain: The storm is now attributed to the arrival of the coronal mass ejection in near-Earth space and its interaction with the Earth's magnetosphere.
